label: Mid-input new token (r/2/k/o/d/h/c...) in sequences starting with b/g/e/q
explanation: Fires only during the original-input phase, never at the delimiter or during copy. It is concentrated at positions t=3..6 (peak at t=4, with ~41% of mass) and almost always on the first occurrence of the current input token. Two token identities shape it. The current input matters: r, 2 and k are strongest, then o, d, h, c, i, n, l. The first token of the sequence also matters: b, g, e and q are strongest, then z, 0, s. The top activations are r/2/k/o inputs at t=4-5 in sequences starting with b or g. It does not fire at t<2 or t>=8, or on repeated tokens (rare). The conjunction captures ~77% of activation mass, but precision is only ~0.43: many matching steps stay silent, so the unit probably depends on a graded combination of earlier tokens that this boolean rule does not capture.
